_comment: Deployment configuration for the fictional Northgate Logistics.
None of these lists have universal defaults. protected_domains decides what
lookalike detection compares against, and trusted_authserv_ids decides which
Authentication-Results header is believed. Both are the difference between a
working detection and a decorative one, so they are configuration rather than
known_senders and allowlisted_domains are synthetic stand-ins for real sender
history. They prove the code path works and nothing more.
trusted_mail_hosts are matched against the 'by' clause of Received headers to find where our estate ends. Below that boundary the chain is whatever the sender chose to write.
